title: Combine the discriminant with a domain-endpoint check to find a range of k for a line meeting a restricted curve
content: When a line y = mx + k must intersect a curve (given in Cartesian or parametric form, but restricted to a limited domain) at two distinct points, there are usually two separate boundaries to find. First, substitute the curve's Cartesian equation into the line equation to get a quadratic in x, and apply the discriminant condition b^2 - 4ac > 0 to find the boundary value of k at which the line is tangent to the curve (beyond this, the line meets the curve at 0 or 2 points depending on direction). Second, separately check what happens when the line passes through the endpoint(s) of the curve's restricted domain — substitute the endpoint's (x, y) coordinates into the line equation to find the k value at which the line just reaches that endpoint. The true range for k combines whichever of these two conditions is actually the binding (tighter) constraint at each end, and you must check the inequality signs carefully (strict where two distinct crossings are required, non-strict where a closed domain endpoint is included).
